      IsOpen {v : RealProjectiveSpace R | realStrictTorsion k v B}

      theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.open_chamber_of_compact_strict (k : Type u) [Field k] {R : Type u} [Ring R] [Algebra k R] [Module.Finite k R] [IsNoetherianRing R] {v : RealProjectiveSpace R} {B : FGModuleCat R} (hb : realStrictTorsion k v = generatedTorsionClass B) :
      ∃ (E : Set (RealProjectiveSpace R)), IsOpen E ∧ E.Nonempty ∧ v ∈ closure E ∧ ∀ w ∈ E, realStrictTorsion k w = realStrictTorsion k v ∧ realWeakTorsion k w = realStrictTorsion k v

      If one module generates the strict numerical torsion class at v, then v is in the closure of a nonempty open set throughout which both numerical torsion classes equal that class.

      theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.subobject_negative_iff_rightOrthogonal (k : Type u) [Field k] {R : Type u} [Ring R] [Algebra k R] [Module.Finite k R] [IsNoetherianRing R] {v : RealProjectiveSpace R} (N : FGModuleCat R) :
      (∀ {U : FGModuleCat R} (i : U ⟶ N) [CategoryTheory.Mono i], ¬CategoryTheory.Limits.IsZero U → (realEulerEvaluation k (GrothendieckGroup.of U)) v < 0) ↔ ∀ (X : FGModuleCat R), realWeakTorsion k v X → Subsingleton (X ⟶ N)

      Strict negativity on each nonzero subobject characterizes the right orthogonal of the weak numerical torsion class.

      theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.open_chamber_of_cocompact_weak (k : Type u) [Field k] {R : Type u} [Ring R] [Algebra k R] [Module.Finite k R] [IsNoetherianRing R] {v : RealProjectiveSpace R} {N : FGModuleCat R} (hn : ∀ (M : FGModuleCat R), realWeakTorsion k v M ↔ Subsingleton (M ⟶ N)) :
      ∃ (E : Set (RealProjectiveSpace R)), IsOpen E ∧ E.Nonempty ∧ v ∈ closure E ∧ ∀ w ∈ E, realStrictTorsion k w = realWeakTorsion k v ∧ realWeakTorsion k w = realWeakTorsion k v

      If the weak class at v is left orthogonal to one module, both numerical classes agree with it on a nonempty open set whose closure contains v.

      theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.bicompact_real_torsion_of_covariantlyFinite (k : Type u) [Field k] {R : Type u} [Ring R] [Algebra k R] [Module.Finite k R] [IsNoetherianRing R] (v : RealProjectiveSpace R) {T : CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty (FGModuleCat R)} (ht : T = realStrictTorsion k v ∨ T = realWeakTorsion k v) (h : CovariantlyFinite T) :
      (∃ (B : FGModuleCat R), T = generatedTorsionClass B) ∧ ∃ (N : FGModuleCat R), ∀ (M : FGModuleCat R), T M ↔ Subsingleton (M ⟶ N)

      Covariant finiteness alone gives both compactness witnesses for either numerical class.
